title: Conjecture 1.1
statement_text: There is a polynomial $P$ such that every graph $G$ that contains no theta, pyramid, prism, or turtle has at most $P(|V(G)|)$ minimal separators.
context_text: Thetas, pyramids, prisms, and turtles each give rise to graphs with exponentially many minimal separators (e.g., $k$-theta, $k$-pyramid, $k$-prism, $k$-turtle). The conjecture asks whether excluding all four is sufficient to obtain a polynomially bounded number of minimal separators, motivating the main theorem of this paper.
paper_contribution: Proves Conjecture 1.1 in full, establishing as Theorem 1.2 that every (theta, pyramid, prism, turtle)-free graph $G$ has at most $|V(G)|^{18}$ minimal separators, constructible in polynomial time.
notes: Reference [7] is cited but the bibliography is not included in the extracted text; attributed year is unknown.
paper_title: Graphs with polynomially many minimal separators

title: Conjecture 1.4
statement_text: There exists $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that if no induced subgraph of $G$ is a $k$-creature, then $G$ has at most $|V(G)|^{f(k)}$ minimal separators.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple. A set $C\subseteq V(G)$ is a minimal separator if $G\setminus C$ has two distinct components $L,R$ with $N(L)=N(R)=C$; a class has the polynomial separator property if for some constant $c$ every member $G$ has at most $|V(G)|^c$ minimal separators (equivalently, polynomially many potential maximal cliques, which makes maximum weight independent set and more generally maximum weight induced subgraph of treewidth less than $k$ polynomial). For an integer $k\ge3$, a $k$-creature is a graph whose vertex set is $A\cup B\cup\{x_1,\dots,x_k\}\cup\{y_1,\dots,y_k\}$ where $G[A]$ and $G[B]$ are connected and $A$ is anticomplete to $B$ (no edges between them); for each $i$, $x_iy_i$ is an edge, $x_i$ has a neighbour in $A$ and none in $B$, and $y_i$ has a neighbour in $B$ and none in $A$; and $x_iy_j$ is not an edge for $i\neq j$ (edges among the $x_i$'s and among the $y_i$'s are unrestricted). Every $k$-creature contains a theta, a pyramid, a prism or a turtle (the paper's four basic configurations of paths forming holes), and the authors prove the conjecture of Chudnovsky, Thomassé, Trotignon and Vušković that graphs with none of these four as induced subgraphs have at most $|V(G)|^{18}$ minimal separators; this conjecture is a stronger generalisation. They prove the weaker version for immature $k$-creatures ($X=\{x_1,\dots,x_k\}$ and $Y=\{y_1,\dots,y_k\}$ with the $x_iy_i$ as the only $X$–$Y$ edges): excluding them gives $O(n^{2k-2})$ minimal separators. Even if true, the conjecture would not characterise the polynomial separator property: induced subgraphs of $k$-turtles with very long paths have it but contain $k$-creatures for arbitrarily large $k$.
notes: The paper proves a weaker version (Theorem 1.5) replacing $k$-creatures by the stricter notion of immature $k$-creatures.
paper_title: Graphs with polynomially many minimal separators
